title: Rivers & coasts
examples: What is the difference between river erosion and coastal erosion?
Can you show me a diagram of a river valley?
How does the river carry away the soil?

explain.say: Today we are learning about how rivers and coasts change over time.

items: Erodes the river bed and banks

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a river from source to sea. Look at the source, the upper course and the tributary. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
River erosion happens when the river wears away the land around it.
When rivers meet the sea, waves constantly attack the coastline.
A waterfall forms when a river flows over different types of rock.

draw.text: Waterfall Formation: Hard rock over soft

explain.say: The process of deposition happens when the river slows down its speed.
In real life, a river valley often has meanders that curve gently.

faq.q: What is the difference between erosion and deposition?
faq.a: Erosion is the process of wearing away material from the land. Deposition is when that worn-away material is dropped somewhere else.
asks: What is the difference between wearing away and dropping off?

faq.q: How does hydraulic action work on a cliff?
faq.a: Hydraulic action is the sheer force of the water compressing air in cracks. This pressure can weaken and break off pieces of rock.
asks: Is hydraulic action about the water's power?
What is the water doing to the rock?

faq.q: Why are waterfalls often found where rock layers change?
faq.a: Waterfalls form because the river meets a layer of hard, resistant rock over softer rock. The soft rock erodes underneath, causing the fall.
asks: Does the rock type matter for waterfalls?
What makes the water drop suddenly?

faq.q: What are meanders in a river?
faq.a: Meanders are the wide, looping bends that a river makes as it flows across a flat area. They show the river is eroding on the outer bank.
asks: What do meanders tell us about the river's energy?

faq.q: What is the role of abrasion in river transport?
faq.a: Abrasion is the scraping action of rocks carried by the river against the river bed. This grinding action smooths and wears down the landscape.
asks: How do rocks wear the river floor?

facts: Rivers erode through hydraulic action, abrasion, and solution.
Coastal erosion is mainly caused by the force of ocean waves.
Waterfalls often form where hard rock overlies soft rock.
Deposition occurs when a river loses energy, usually by slowing down.

quiz.say: If a river flows over soft rock covered by hard rock, what feature is most likely to form?
quiz.why: The hard rock resists erosion while the softer rock underneath erodes more quickly.

wrong.0: Meanders form in the middle of a river, not necessarily at a change in rock type.
wrong.1: Sea arches form along coastlines due to wave action, not river flow.
wrong.2: Flood plains are areas of deposition, but not the direct result of the rock change.

quiz.say: Which process involves the force of the water itself hitting the rock?
quiz.why: Hydraulic action is the physical force of the water compressing air in cracks.

wrong.0: Abrasion is caused by the scraping of rocks carried by the water.
wrong.1: Solution involves dissolving minerals in the water, not physical force.
wrong.2: Deposition is the dropping of material, which is the result, not the force itself.

quiz.say: When a river slows down its speed, what material is most likely to be left behind?
quiz.why: When the river loses energy, it can no longer carry its load, so it drops the sediment.

wrong.0: Sea cliffs are formed by wave action on coastlines, not by river slowing down.
wrong.1: Meanders are bends in the river path, not the material left behind.
wrong.2: Waterfalls are formed by differences in rock resistance, not by slowing down.
